new_entities.name: CPAP for severe obstructive sleep apnea
aliases: continuous positive airway pressure for severe OSA
CPAP in severe obstructive sleep apnea
new_entities.description: Continuous positive airway pressure treatment used in adults with severe or at least moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea.

new_entities.name: Daytime sleepiness
new_entities.description: Daytime sleepiness or reduced wakefulness during usual waking hours.

edges.effect_quant: CPAP reliably improves sleepiness symptoms in moderate-severe OSA: a 41-RCT meta-analysis found ESS WMD -2.14, SAVE reported significant sleepiness improvement, and another 18-trial meta-analysis found ESS MD -1.78.
edges.population: adults with severe or at least moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea, especially those with elevated baseline Epworth scores and reasonable nightly adherence
edges.mechanism: By preventing recurrent upper-airway collapse, CPAP reduces arousals, restores sleep continuity, and reduces nocturnal hypoxemia, which together lessen excessive daytime sleepiness.
edges.summary: This is one of the strongest CPAP edges. Even when cardiovascular outcomes stay neutral, symptom relief for daytime sleepiness is consistent and clinically meaningful.
edges.caveats: Benefits are smaller in mild OSA, in minimally sleepy populations, and when nightly adherence is short. Some individual trials report stronger benefit in sleepier subgroups than in the whole cohort.

evidence.notes: Predictors of the Efficacy for Daytime Sleepiness in Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea With Continual Positive Airway Pressure Therapy: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
